name: Two-Connected Terminal Towers over Cut-Vertex Seeds
statement: Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded, corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor with a cut vertex. Suppose $a,b\notin S$ are distinct resolving tips such that $S\cup\{a\}$ and $S\cup\{b\}$ are dismantlable ample and acquire distinct shattered supports. For every nonempty coordinate set $E$ disjoint from $F$, put $X_E=(S\times Q_E)\cup(\{a\}\times(Q_E\setminus\{0^E\}))\cup(\{b\}\times(Q_E\setminus\{1^E\}))$. Then $X_E$ is a two-connected, corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor. Its unique largest successful layer set is exactly $E$, and $X_E^E=S$. If $S$ has corners, no successful layer choice for $X_E$ has a cornerless recovered seed. Moreover, $X_E$ has minimum degree at least three and equals its graph three-core.
proof: The two antipodally punctured occurrence rows partition the signed facets, so the common-seed construction and seed-corner deletion criterion make $X_E$ ample, forbidden, and terminal; the replicated construction is two-connected. The displayed presentation makes $E$ successful with reduction $S$. If the largest successful set $D$ satisfied $E\subsetneq D$, strong projection from its recovered presentation along $E$ would retain a nontrivial signed-facet assembly over $D\setminus E$ with at least two distinct resolving tips. This would present $S$ as a two-connected replicated construction, contradicting its cut vertex. Thus $D=E$. Cornerless recovery can only occur at the largest successful set, so a cornered $S$ rules it out. A terminal ample obstruction has no vertex of degree at most two: the low-degree theorem would otherwise provide an obstruction-preserving corner deletion. Hence $X_E$ is its three-core.
comments: This gives two-connected terminal counterexamples to cornerlessness of the canonical largest recovered seed, even after graph two-core pruning. The construction still has a successful layer set; the following edge-amalgam family removes layer recovery altogether.
